collections.label: DOORS Hotel starter reference
collections.note: 12 selected threats and supplies for ordinary Hotel runs on PC and mobile. Not a complete DOORS encyclopedia. Modifiers and other floors can change these rules. Community article text was checked through the search index; direct Fandom access was blocked.

entries.name: Ambush
entries.summary: A rushing threat that can return after passing.
body: Stay close to a hiding place between passes.

entries.name: Eyes
entries.summary: A glowing cluster that hurts players who look at it.
body: Different entities require different responses.

entries.name: Dupe
entries.summary: False numbered doors punish careless entry.
body: Track the sequence as you enter each room.

entries.name: Figure
entries.summary: A major Hotel threat encountered in the Library and Electrical Room.
facts: Temporary stun, not a full banish
body: Watch its route and keep space. Crouching is not permission to walk into Figure or remain directly in its path.

entries.name: Halt
entries.summary: An encounter that asks you to change direction as it blocks the route.
body: Follow the encounter cues instead of relying on a fixed room number or an old guaranteed-spawn claim.

entries.name: Timothy
entries.summary: A small spider jumps from a looted container and briefly startles the player.
body: Timothy is a looting hazard, not a hallway chase. Recover your view and continue checking the room for other threats.

entries.name: Room Key
entries.summary: A key belongs to a specific locked door.
body: Search accessible areas before spending another tool. A scrambled label during Dupe is not a reliable shortcut to the correct exit.

entries.name: Lockpick
entries.summary: A consumable tool can bypass many ordinary locks.
body: It is useful when finding a normal room key would take time. Check the type of lock before expecting it to work.

entries.name: Flashlight
entries.summary: A directional light that needs battery charge.
body: Save charge for dark sections. An empty flashlight needs batteries rather than repeated attempts to switch it on.

entries.name: Lighter
entries.summary: A small fuel-based light for nearby surroundings.
body: Turn it off when light is unnecessary. Lighting it can make sound, so consider nearby threats before using it.

entries.name: Vitamins
entries.summary: A consumable gives a temporary movement-speed boost.
body: Use the speed for a planned route. It does not replace learning a chase path or watching obstacles.

entries.name: Crucifix
entries.summary: A held defensive item can restrain eligible entities.
facts: Seek and Figure only briefly stunned
body: Keep moving during a boss stun. A temporary restraint is not a completed chase or permission to stand beside the boss.

collections.label: PUBG PC starter reference
collections.note: 12 selected weapon families and maps from the publisher directory. This is not a full weapon-stat database or a current map-rotation list. Individual ammo, attachments, balance and availability should be checked in-game.

entries.name: Assault rifles (AR)
entries.summary: A flexible weapon family suited to many middle-distance fights.
body: Use the official family list to identify a weapon, then inspect the actual gun and compatible ammunition in the current game. Family membership alone does not make every rifle handle the same.

entries.name: Designated marksman rifles (DMR)
entries.summary: A family intended for controlled attacks at middle and longer distances.
body: This category helps separate a range-focused weapon from a close-range option when planning a loadout. Compare the actual item rather than assuming all DMRs share ammunition.

entries.name: Submachine guns (SMG)
entries.summary: A family associated with mobility and quick fire in close fights.
body: Recognize the category when deciding what role a pickup fills. Close-range usefulness does not make it the right choice for every distant target.

entries.name: Sniper rifles (SR)
entries.summary: A range-focused family built around accurate, powerful shots.
body: Use the family as a starting point for comparison. Read the weapon and ammunition information rather than expecting identical firing behaviour across the whole category.

entries.name: Shotguns
entries.summary: A family suited to sudden close encounters.
body: Learn the particular shotgun before rushing a doorway. The official directory groups several designs here; their reload and firing behaviour need individual practice.

entries.name: Handguns
entries.summary: Compact secondary firearms provide another equipment option.
body: Check the equipped item rather than assuming every handgun fires the same way. The directory includes both pistol and revolver designs.

entries.name: Melee weapons
entries.summary: Hand-held weapons are used at contact distance.
body: The short reach is the key difference from firearms. Do not approach a distant opponent expecting the same options as a ranged weapon.

entries.name: Throwables
entries.summary: Thrown utility offers different ways to pressure opponents or create cover.
body: Read the item name before using it. The throwable category includes tools with very different purposes; a smoke and a frag are not interchangeable.

entries.name: Special weapons
entries.summary: The official ETC directory groups equipment beyond the main firearm families.
body: This is a mixed directory, not one shared firing style. Read each item’s controls and availability before building a plan around it.

entries.name: Erangel
entries.summary: An island combining open grassland, mountains and built-up settlements.
body: Compare open ground with nearby buildings before choosing a route. This is a map introduction, not a promise that Erangel is in every current queue.

entries.name: Miramar
entries.summary: A desert battleground with exposed terrain and long sightlines.
body: Consider where cover ends before crossing barren ground. The official overview highlights its suitability for snipers; that does not prescribe one mandatory loadout.

entries.name: Taego
entries.summary: A large map with varied terrain and landmarks including Ho San Prison.
body: Use the live match map to plan a route between the current circle and nearby terrain. Queue availability and special mechanics are separate from this basic map reference.

collections.label: Wuthering Waves starter reference
collections.note: 12 selected attributes, weapon families and progression terms. This is not a complete character roster, build ranking or item database. Community article text was checked through the search index; no in-game combat test was performed.

entries.name: Glacio
entries.summary: An attribute associated with cooling and freezing.
body: An attribute labels damage and related effects. Read the specific skill instead of assuming every Glacio attack automatically applies a status.

entries.name: Fusion
entries.summary: An attribute associated with heat and ignition.
body: Weapon family and attribute are separate labels. Read a skill’s actual effect before choosing gear for it.

entries.name: Electro
entries.summary: An attribute associated with electrical charge.
body: Only attacks with the relevant effect apply Electro Flare; the attribute label alone is not a full skill description.

entries.name: Aero
body: Aero Erosion is a status associated with certain attacks and effects. Check the skill text rather than expecting every Aero hit to apply it.

entries.name: Spectro
entries.summary: An attribute associated with light and photons.
body: Spectro Frazzle is a stacking effect used by particular abilities. Do not infer an entire rotation from the attribute icon.

entries.name: Havoc
body: Havoc Bane is a particular status effect, not a guarantee attached to every Havoc attack. Read the ability or encounter rule that applies it.

entries.name: Sword
entries.summary: One equipment family with several different secondary-stat options.
body: Choose between actual effects and stat needs. The shared Sword label does not make these items equivalent.

entries.name: Broadblade
entries.summary: A weapon family used by Resonators such as Jiyan and Taoqi.
body: The same family includes different secondary stats. Compare the character’s needs before investing in one.

entries.name: Pistols
entries.summary: A weapon category with damage-focused and utility-focused options.
body: Compare the item effect as well as its stat.

entries.name: Gauntlets
entries.summary: A weapon category whose items can support different stat needs.
body: Match the item to the Resonator’s actual scaling.

entries.name: Rectifier
entries.summary: An equipment family containing both damage and support-oriented stat options.
body: A shared family does not imply the same role. Compare the weapon’s full effect before equipping it.

entries.name: Data Bank
entries.summary: The Terminal system records Echo discoveries and affects Echo collection progression.
body: Check your own Data Bank screen for current level requirements. Repeating an already-recorded rarity is different from discovering a new entry; old level-cap tables may no longer apply.
